title: Surge Pricing
summary: Precompute stable per-cell surge multipliers from demand and supply while honoring accepted fare quotes.
narrative:
Raise fares where rider demand outstrips available drivers to attract supply and ration rides, while keeping prices stable and honoring a fare the rider accepted. Divide cities into H3 hexagonal cells about 1–2 km across. Across ~500 K active cells, ingest ~1.25 M driver pings/s plus ~50 K quote events/s. Recompute each cell's multiplier every 60 s; the quote API serves ~50 K reads/s with p99 < 50 ms. Driver apps show a heatmap from the same per-cell multiplier map.

Clients send pings, fare quotes and ride requests through a Load Balancer to redundant Web Servers. Append supply and demand events to a Message Queue. Redundant Stream Processors count available drivers and demand signals over per-cell sliding windows, distinguishing repeated quotes from unique requests and expiring stale driver availability. An ML Model Server maps the demand/supply ratio, short-term demand forecast, events and weather to a multiplier. Define safe behavior for zero supply, smooth changes with EWMA, and apply hysteresis and caps to avoid oscillation. Store the versioned multiplier per cell in Cache with an expiry; when it expires, use a defined safe fallback rather than indefinitely serving stale surge.

Compute surge away from the quote request. The Web Server reads the pickup cell's precomputed multiplier, returns the fare, and stores a locked quote in SQL with its price, multiplier version and ~2 min expiry. Accepting a still-valid quote conditionally associates that price with the trip; a later multiplier change must not reprice it, and an expired quote requires a fresh offer. Dispatch stays unchanged. For audit, analytics and regulators, each locked quote records the multiplier version it used, and the retained demand/supply event log plus the versioned model let every multiplier be reproduced. Optionally archive that log in a Data Warehouse for long-term pricing analysis, and monitor stale cells, demand/supply lag and price oscillation.

functional: Aggregate demand and available-driver supply in sliding windows per H3 cell
Compute multipliers every 60 s using ratio, forecast, events and weather; apply EWMA, hysteresis and caps
Write expiring versioned multipliers to Cache and serve quote reads and driver heatmaps from that map
Store locked quotes and trips in SQL; honor accepted prices for valid ~2 min quotes without changing dispatch
Record the multiplier version used by every locked quote and retain the demand/supply event log and model version so multiplier changes can be audited and reproduced for analytics and regulators
nonFunctional: Ingest ~1.25 M pings/s plus ~50 K quote events/s across ~500 K active cells
Serve ~50 K quote reads/s with p99 < 50 ms without synchronous model inference
Continue after a Web Server or Stream Processor failure; bound stale surge and price oscillation
constraints: Web Servers must never call the ML Model Server on the quote path; read precomputed Cache multipliers
All Web Server paths to Stream Processors must pass through Message Queue
Connect Stream Processors to Cache; define multiplier expiry, zero-supply handling and a safe fallback
Validate quote identity and expiry on acceptance and preserve its locked price in SQL
capacity: ~500 K active H3 cells, each about 1–2 km; multiplier refresh every 60 s
~1.25 M driver pings/s + ~50 K quote events/s ≈ 1.30 M input events/s
~50 K quote reads/s, p99 < 50 ms; locked quote validity ~2 min
specs.tradeoff: Minute-scale precomputation keeps quote reads fast but lags sudden demand. Smaller cells improve local sensitivity while sparse samples increase noise; smoothing and hysteresis reduce flapping at the cost of slower response. Locked quotes preserve trust while temporarily diverging from the latest multiplier.
specs.bonus: Connect Message Queue → Data Warehouse for audit and pricing analytics, and add Monitoring for freshness and unstable multipliers.

missions.label: Route ride traffic through the Load Balancer
Predict surge from demand and supply
Retain pricing events for audit and analysis

topologyRules.message: Don't compute surge on the quote path — read the precomputed multiplier.
Buffer demand and supply events in Message Queue before per-cell processing.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two Web Servers so quotes remain available after one failure.
Run at least two Stream Processors so multiplier updates survive an instance failure.
Connect Stream Processors to Cache to publish precomputed cell multipliers.

hints: Start with Client → Load Balancer → Web Server. Connect Web Server → Cache for multiplier reads and → SQL Database for locked quotes; compute surge separately from these reads.

Wire Web Server → Message Queue → Stream Processor, then Stream Processor → ML Model Server and → Cache. Aggregate per-cell windows, smooth predictions and expire stale multipliers; keep model calls off the Web Server path.

Run two Web Servers and two Stream Processors. Each Web Server reaches Message Queue, Cache and SQL; the queue feeds both processors, each connected to the model server and Cache. Add Message Queue → Data Warehouse and each Web Server → Monitoring.
